selection: Focused primary research and official technical sources; metrics are not pooled with this study.

sources.citation: J. Elson, L. Girod and D. Estrin. Fine-Grained Network Time Synchronization Using Reference Broadcasts. OSDI, 2002.
sources.finding: Receivers compare the arrival of a shared broadcast, avoiding some sender-side uncertainty. Relative synchronization and externally referenced time are distinct use cases.
sources.relevance: Motivates event-level observations and careful separation of relative consistency from external UTC. The current watch uses authenticated source-to-receiver models, not an implementation of RBS.

sources.citation: M. Maroti, B. Kusy, G. Simon and A. Ledeczi. The Flooding Time Synchronization Protocol. SenSys, 2004, pp. 39-49.
sources.finding: Low-level timestamping and regression of previous observations estimate skew and offset. Root-election transitions preserve learned time, and the paper separately examines drift after synchronization stops.
sources.relevance: Continuity through source changes and learned-rate holdover are established ideas. This study's narrower contribution is a dual-radio service policy and causal GNSS-free measurement contract with explicit authentication and expiry.

sources.citation: K. S. Yildirim, R. Carli and L. Schenato. Proportional-Integral Clock Synchronization in Wireless Sensor Networks. arXiv:1410.8176, 2014.
sources.finding: PI feedback compensates clock phase and speed differences, with flooding and distributed implementations, analysis, simulations and physical experiments.
sources.relevance: Supports treating timekeeping as a phase/rate control problem. It does not validate the gains, sparse LoRa rate law or holdover performance of this watch.

sources.citation: S. Sridhar, P. Misra, G. S. Gill and J. Warrior. CheepSync: A Time Synchronization Service for Resource Constrained Bluetooth Low Energy Advertisers. IEEE Communications Magazine 54(1), 2016, pp. 136-143.
sources.finding: BLE advertiser synchronization uses low-level timestamping and compensation for transmission and clock uncertainties, evaluated on beacon hardware and passive smartphone listeners.
sources.relevance: BLE timing predates this study. Different BLE versions, event markers, devices and reference methods prevent a direct accuracy ranking.

sources.citation: C. G. Ramirez, A. Sergeyev, A. Dyussenova and B. Iannucci. LongShoT: Long-Range Synchronization of Time. IPSN, 2019. DOI:10.1145/3302506.3310408.
sources.finding: LoRaWAN timing combines hardware/MAC-level timestamps with oscillator-drift compensation and evaluates distributed devices against GPS 1PPS.
sources.relevance: Shows why sparse long-range observations and drift compensation matter. Its network transactions and independent GPS witness differ from passive authenticated LoRa fallback here. The primary repository's searchable paper text was available; repeated direct PDF fetches returned HTTP 502.

sources.citation: S. Rinaldi, E. Mondini, P. Ferrari, A. Flammini and E. Sisinni. LoRa/LoRaWAN Time Synchronization: A Comprehensive Analysis, Performance Evaluation, and Compensation of Frame Timestamping. Future Internet 18(2), 80, 2026. DOI:10.3390/fi18020080.
sources.finding: A raw-IQ matched-filter simulation separates sampling phase, frequency mismatch and noise. Longer chirps increase systematic sensitivity to sampling-frequency offset; dispersion and bias are distinct.
sources.relevance: A fixed receiver engineering correction is not portable calibration. This simulation does not characterize the watch's SX1262 HeaderValid edge, propagation or field multipath.

sources.citation: D. Mills, J. Martin, J. Burbank and W. Kasch. Network Time Protocol Version 4: Protocol and Algorithms Specification. RFC 5905, 2010, sections 11-12.
sources.finding: NTP separates clock-source selection, clustering and combination from the oscillator discipline process. Its combination algorithm averages surviving candidates.
sources.relevance: Provides useful terminology, not a claim of NTP conformance. The watch's priority/complementary controller is different from simultaneous statistical combination; shared GM paths are not independent references.

sources.citation: W. J. Riley and D. A. Howe. Handbook of Frequency Stability Analysis. NIST Special Publication 1065, 2008.
sources.finding: Describes frequency-stability definitions, measurement systems, data handling, analysis methods and reporting.
sources.relevance: Guides later witness-based oscillator characterization. A short, switched, correlated controller-input series is not an independent Allan-deviation or holdover-accuracy qualification.

sources.citation: Bluetooth SIG. Bluetooth Core Specification 6.1, Generic Access Profile, section 9.5, Periodic Advertising.
sources.finding: Periodic-advertising synchronization establishes reception of a periodic train using discovery or transferred synchronization information.
sources.relevance: Controller PA synchronization is a link-reception state. It is not application authentication, valid UTC, receiver quality or a calibrated clock bound.
